We're coming up on our renewal window for HelioCorp (annual deal, currently with Redwood since 2024). We ran an internal usage run-rate review and want to propose the following for the next 12 months:

Can your team confirm whether these are acceptable and who on your legal side should review redlines? We'd like to keep to a 2-week turnaround if possible — target signature by 2026-10-01.

Lauren / Team / Olivia — quick legal read and proposed next steps. I've uploaded a tracked-changes draft (redlines_mk.docx). Summary of material points and suggested language: 

1) Liability cap: we will propose 1x annualized fees (not 2x) with a narrow carveout for breach of confidentiality and willful misconduct. Suggested fallback phrase: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer's aggregate liability for damages under this Agreement shall not exceed the amount of Fees paid to Supplier during the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, except that such cap shall not apply to willful misconduct or a breach of confidentiality obligations."

2) Cache retention: ops confirms we can set production KV retention to 30 days for Helio but recommend an addendum that clarifies the data scope (i.e., does not affect feature-store backups or long-term observability logs). I propose we add a short Security Addendum clause rather than changing the MSA's data retention section.

3) Staggered billing & invoicing: commercial can support monthly invoices for months 1–6, but Finance wants a clause allowing early termination for non-payment and a 10% deposit for the ramp portion. Proposed language appended in the doc.

4) Extension option: legal is comfortable with an 18-month extension option exercised with 30 days' notice, but we should preserve rate review language — e.g., "Customer may exercise an extension option for an additional eighteen (18) months upon sixty (60) days prior written notice; pricing during the extension shall be subject to mutual agreement, provided that Supplier will not increase unit pricing within the first six (6) months of the extension without written consent."

Procurement note: If Helio insists on 2x ARR liability cap, we'll need to escalate to Sales Leadership for credit risk approval. Also flagging that the +40% burst will require a transient buffer capacity reservation and potentially a short-term surcharge.

I'll be on the 9/20 call. Attaching: redlines_mk.docx (tracked changes + suggested short clauses).

-Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
